title: Retell a life chapter with agency and circumstance

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A life narrative selects events and meaning. A fair revision adds agency, constraint and received help without turning every loss into growth or every contribution into solitary heroism.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional chapter: before joining a drawing group, Rae practiced alone using a borrowed pencil and free library pages. At the turning point a friend offered two specific shading corrections; Rae practiced them for three evenings. Now Rae can shade one simple form but still finds proportion difficult. One exhibition invitation was missed because transport was unavailable. No award or further feedback exists.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write before/turning-point/now, separating events from interpretation. Correct “I mastered drawing alone” without erasing Rae’s effort or the missed opportunity.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A narrative accurately names a structural barrier but omits the person’s actual preparation and request for help. What can be added without blaming them for the barrier?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A fair account credits practice, borrowed materials and feedback, limits the skill to one form and retains the transport loss. Partial: add help but still claim mastery. Incorrect: recast the missed exhibition as necessary for growth without evidence. Later fiction: Rae accepts an accessible text demonstration and makes one improved form; long-term development remains unknown.
criteria: Remaining difficulty or loss is retained

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Add those actions as agency within the constraint. They neither caused nor removed every external condition; a richer narrative need not choose between total hero and total victim.
criteria: Remaining difficulty or loss is retained
